chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn Khalid from someone who narrated to him, from al-Mufadhdhal ibn Umar. Al-Kulayni said: And Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from his father from some of his men, from al-Mufadhdhal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

The servants are closest to Allah and most pleasing to Him when they miss the Proof of Allah and he does not appear to them, nor do they know his location, and while in that state they know that the Proof of Allah, exalted is His mention, and His covenant have not been annulled. So anticipate the relief morning and evening, for the harshest anger of Allah will be upon His enemies when they miss the Proof of Allah and he does not appear to them. And Allah has known that His friends will not doubt; and if He knew that they would doubt, He would not hide His Proof from them for the blink of an eye. And that will not be except for the worst of people.

key_terms.الْفَرَج: The relief/deliverance (referring to the reappearance of the Imam)
key_terms.حُجَّةُ اللَّهِ: The Proof of Allah (referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: Why are believers closest to Allah during the occultation of the Imam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that the peak of divine proximity and pleasure occurs during the occultation, as believers maintain certainty that the 'Proof of Allah' remains active despite being unseen. This period of hiddenness serves as a test of faith, where Allah ensures the Imam is not concealed even for a moment if He knew the faithful would waver, thereby distinguishing true believers from the 'worst of people' who succumb to doubt.
